acceptance_mapping.statement: Protection completes only when all three required layers have pairwise-distinct failure-domain identities.
Every layer representation verifies to the same qualified byte identity.
Operational SQL success alone never establishes backup or recovery readiness.
Recovery journal events are immutable and append-only.
Archive objects and manifests are content-addressed and never overwritten.
A restore candidate is never a verified restoration.
Restoration requires destination retrieval and exact verification for the closed object set.
Database dialect, placeholders, binary types, adapter, and connection protocol never enter object identity.
PostgreSQL is the first conforming adapter and cannot become the SQL portability contract.
Any missing layer, shared failure domain, mismatch, incomplete set, or unavailable source yields typed failure and no success.
Plaintext, unwrapped keys, private keys, and credentials are excluded from every layer and evidence record.
Protection and recovery claims are bounded to exact realizations, policies, failure domains, object sets, and observation intervals.

exclusions: treating three copies inside one effective failure domain as three-layer protection
making PostgreSQL, SQL dialect, container, volume, provider, or locator identity part of immutable object identity
using PostgreSQL WAL, physical database pages, or vendor dumps as the portable recovery authority
claiming backup completion without exact object identity closure across all required layers
claiming restoration from copy, replay, import, process start, or query success without destination retrieval and verification
storing plaintext, unwrapped content keys, private keys, or credentials
selecting production topology, region, credentials, retention, RPO, RTO, publication, release, or deployment
capability.outcome: For one exact encrypted knowledge-material object, establish verified protection across an operational SQL layer, an independently failed recovery-journal layer, and an immutable SQL-independent archive layer; then reconstruct and verify the object into any conforming SQL realization without confusing copy, replay, import, or database startup with restoration proof.

limitations: Description import only; PostgreSQL, Docker, archive and recovery tests were not run. Semantic contract identities resolve but do not prove operational restoration.
Credit release, inventory reservation and production rollback remain reference examples, not capabilities.
notes: Product boundary and declared owner completed from its explicit source Product Thesis.
Source lifecycle preserved verbatim; candidate storage does not activate it.
Realization references preserved as unverified source metadata; no realization asserted.
